content.content:
---
name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e7324b18-29e9-4db0-ae5a-a9f0cd196a49
  modified: 2026-10-16T18:23:14.513Z
---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. Qwen2.5-14B bf16 (~30 GB) won't fit when GPUs have ≤23 GB free.

Update 2026-10-16 (system_prompt_residual_effects workspace): the neurico runner can kill a session at its 6h limit (return_code 143) and relaunch with the same prompt while detached background jobs (e.g. `run_all.sh`) keep running. On start, check for existing planning.md/REPORT.md, `*_PLACEHOLDER` markers, `.neurico/pipeline_*.json`, `*.partial` checkpoints and live PIDs before redoing anything; usually you only need to wait for the jobs and re-run the scoring/analysis.

Update 2026-10-19 (instruction-length workspace): GPU free memory can drop to ≤5 GB on *all* 4 GPUs for hours (other users' jobs) — run the biggest/most important models FIRST while a GPU is free, and run small models (≤1.5B, ~5 GB) in parallel on leftover slices. idea:
  title: "In-Context Learning Label Bias: When Demonstrations Teach the Wrong Lesson"
  description: >
    In-context learning (ICL) can pick up spurious correlations from
    few-shot demonstrations, such as label frequency imbalance or
    positional patterns. This study isolates and quantifies four types
    of label bias that few-shot demonstrations introduce, measuring
    how each one distorts predictions independently of task knowledge.

    We construct controlled demonstration sets for 4 NLU tasks
    (sentiment, NLI, topic classification, paraphrase detection) with
    5 bias manipulations: (1) label frequency skew (80/20 vs 50/50),
    (2) recency bias (last 2 examples share a label), (3) label-length
    correlation (positive examples are longer), (4) label-position
    correlation (label always near sentence start), and (5) a clean
    baseline. We test across 4 model sizes (0.5B to 14B) measuring
    accuracy, calibration error, and prediction entropy.

    Use locally runnable models via Ollama. Write a computational
    paper under 3000 words with 2-3 figures.
  hypothesis: >
    Label frequency skew produces the largest bias (15-25% accuracy
    shift toward the majority label), followed by recency bias (8-15%).
    Label-length correlation has moderate effect (5-10%) and is harder
    for models to overcome with scale. Larger models partially correct
    frequency skew but amplify recency bias. Calibration error
    increases monotonically with all bias types.
  domain: artificial_intelligence
  references:
    - "Zhao et al. (2021) Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models"
    - "Fei et al. (2023) Mitigating Label Biases for In-context Learning"

mkdir -p /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/icl_label_bias_20261020_001001_e5f6g7h8/{src,figures,results/raw,datasets/prompts}; cat > /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/icl_label_bias_20261020_001001_e5f6g7h8/src/build_prompts.py <<'EOF'
"""Build controlled few-shot prompts for the ICL label-bias study.

For each task we draw a fixed evaluation set (balanced over gold labels) and,
for every (test example, target label T, condition), a fresh k=10 demonstration
set from the training split.  The "target label" T is the label favoured by the
manipulation; T is rotated through every label so that a model's prior label
preference cancels out when we average shifts.

Conditions
  clean    : balanced label counts (5/5, or 3/3/2/2 for 4-way), random order
  skew     : 8 of 10 demos carry T (80/20)
  recency  : balanced counts, the last 2 demos carry T
  primacy  : balanced counts, the first 2 demos carry T   (label-position)
  length   : balanced counts, T demos drawn from the longest third of the
             T pool, non-T demos from the shortest third of their pools
All prompts are written to datasets/prompts/prompts.jsonl and are shared by
every model, so comparisons across models are fully paired.
"""
import json, hashlib, random, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
HUB = "/data/transformers/hub"
K = 10
N_TEST_PER_TASK = 200
CONDITIONS = ["clean", "skew", "recency", "primacy", "length"]


def _snap(repo):
    d = f"{HUB}/datasets--{repo}/snapshots"
    return os.path.join(d, sorted(os.listdir(d))[0], "data")


def load_tasks():
    """Return dict task -> (train_df, test_df, spec). Each df has text fields,
    `label` (int) and `nwords` (length used for the length manipulation)."""
    tasks = {}
    sst = _snap("stanfordnlp--sst2")
    tr = pd.read_parquet(f"{sst}/train-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"sentence": "x"})
    te = pd.read_parquet(f"{sst}/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"sentence": "x"})
    tr["x"] = tr.x.str.strip(); te["x"] = te.x.str.strip()
    tasks["sst2"] = (tr, te, dict(
        instr="Classify the sentiment of each movie review as positive or negative.",
        fields=[("Review", "x")], answer="Sentiment", labels=["negative", "positive"]))

    ag = _snap("fancyzhx--ag_news")
    tr = pd.read_parquet(f"{ag}/train-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"text": "x"})
    te = pd.read_parquet(f"{ag}/test-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"text": "x"})
    tasks["agnews"] = (tr, te, dict(
        instr="Classify the topic of each news article as World, Sports, Business, or Technology.",
        fields=[("Article", "x")], answer="Topic",
        labels=["World", "Sports", "Business", "Technology"]))

    for t, instr, f1, f2, ans, labels in [
        ("rte", "Decide whether the premise entails the hypothesis (yes or no).",

    df["frac_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["last2_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d[-2:]) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["first2_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d[:2]) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]

                              for nw, d, T in zip(df.demo_nwords, df.demo_labels, df["T"])]

"""Build controlled few-shot prompts for the ICL label-bias study.

For each task we draw a fixed evaluation set (balanced over gold labels) and,
for every (test example, target label T, condition), a fresh k=10 demonstration
set from the training split.  The "target label" T is the label favoured by the
manipulation; T is rotated through every label so that a model's prior label
preference cancels out when we average shifts.

Conditions
  clean    : balanced label counts (5/5, or 3/3/2/2 for 4-way), random order
  skew     : 8 of 10 demos carry T (80/20)
  recency  : balanced counts, the last 2 demos carry T
  primacy  : balanced counts, the first 2 demos carry T   (label-position)
  length   : balanced counts, T demos drawn from the longest third of the
             T pool, non-T demos from the shortest third of their pools
All prompts are written to datasets/prompts/prompts.jsonl and are shared by
every model, so comparisons across models are fully paired.
"""
import json, hashlib, random, os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
HUB = "/data/transformers/hub"
K = 10
N_TEST_PER_TASK = 200
CONDITIONS = ["clean", "skew", "recency", "primacy", "length"]


def _snap(repo):
    d = f"{HUB}/datasets--{repo}/snapshots"
    return os.path.join(d, sorted(os.listdir(d))[0], "data")


def load_tasks():
    """Return dict task -> (train_df, test_df, spec). Each df has text fields,
    `label` (int) and `nwords` (length used for the length manipulation)."""
    tasks = {}
    sst = _snap("stanfordnlp--sst2")
    tr = pd.read_parquet(f"{sst}/train-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"sentence": "x"})
    te = pd.read_parquet(f"{sst}/validation-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"sentence": "x"})
    tr["x"] = tr.x.str.strip(); te["x"] = te.x.str.strip()
    tasks["sst2"] = (tr, te, dict(
        instr="Classify the sentiment of each movie review as positive or negative.",
        fields=[("Review", "x")], answer="Sentiment", labels=["negative", "positive"]))

    ag = _snap("fancyzhx--ag_news")
    tr = pd.read_parquet(f"{ag}/train-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"text": "x"})
    te = pd.read_parquet(f"{ag}/test-00000-of-00001.parquet").rename(columns={"text": "x"})
    tasks["agnews"] = (tr, te, dict(
        instr="Classify the topic of each news article as World, Sports, Business, or Technology.",
        fields=[("Article", "x")], answer="Topic",
        labels=["World", "Sports", "Business", "Technology"]))

    for t, instr, f1, f2, ans, labels in [
        ("rte", "Decide whether the premise entails the hypothesis (yes or no).",
         "Premise", "Hypothesis", "Entailment", ["yes", "no"]),  # 0=entailment
        ("mrpc", "Decide whether the two sentences are paraphrases of each other (yes or no).",
         "Sentence 1", "Sentence 2", "Paraphrase", ["no", "yes"]),  # 1=equivalent
    ]:
        tr = pd.read_parquet(f"{ROOT}/datasets/raw/{t}/train.parquet")
        te = pd.read_parquet(f"{ROOT}/datasets/raw/{t}/validation.parquet")
        tasks[t] = (tr, te, dict(instr=instr, fields=[(f1, "sentence1"), (f2, "sentence2")],
                                 answer=ans, labels=labels))

    for t, (tr, te, spec) in tasks.items():
        for df in (tr, te):
            df["nwords"] = sum(df[c].str.split().str.len() for _, c in spec["fields"])
        # keep demo pool to reasonable lengths so prompts stay < ~2k tokens
        lo = 5 if t == "sst2" else 1
        hi = {"sst2": 60, "agnews": 80, "rte": 80, "mrpc": 70}[t]
        tr = tr[(tr.nwords >= lo) & (tr.nwords <= hi)].reset_index(drop=True)
        te = te[(te.nwords <= hi * 1.5)].reset_index(drop=True)
        tasks[t] = (tr, te, spec)
    return tasks


def seed_of(*parts):
    return int(hashlib.md5("|".join(map(str, parts)).encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16)


def fmt_example(row, spec, with_label=True):
    s = "".join(f"{name}: {row[col]}\n" for name, col in spec["fields"])
    s += f"{spec['answer']}:"
    if with_label:
        s += f" {spec['labels'][int(row['label'])]}\n\n"
    return s


def label_counts(n_labels, T, cond, rng):
    """Number of demos per label for a given condition."""
    if cond == "skew":
        counts = [0] * n_labels
        counts[T] = 8
        others = [l for l in range(n_labels) if l != T]
        for l in rng.choice(others, size=K - 8, replace=len(others) < K - 8):
            counts[l] += 1
        return counts
    if n_labels == 2:
        return [5, 5]
    base = [3, 3, 2, 2]  # 4-way: random which two labels get 3
    rng.shuffle(base)
    return base


def build_demos(train, spec, T, cond, rng, length_pools):
    n_labels = len(spec["labels"])
    counts = label_counts(n_labels, T, cond, rng)
    if n_labels == 4 and cond in ("recency", "primacy") and counts[T] < 2:
        # make sure T can fill the 2 designated slots (swap with a 3-label)
        j = int(np.argmax(counts)); counts[T], counts[j] = counts[j], counts[T]
    demos = []
    for l, c in enumerate(counts):
        if c == 0:
            continue
        if cond == "length":
            pool = length_pools[l]["long" if l == T else "short"]
        else:
            pool = length_pools[l]["all"]
        idx = rng.choice(pool, size=c, replace=False)
        demos += [train.iloc[i] for i in idx]
    order = rng.permutation(len(demos))
    demos = [demos[i] for i in order]
    if cond in ("recency", "primacy"):
        tdem = [d for d in demos if int(d.label) == T]
        rest = [d for d in demos if int(d.label) != T]
        fixed, rest = tdem[:2], tdem[2:] + rest
        rest = [rest[i] for i in rng.permutation(len(rest))]
        demos = rest + fixed if cond == "recency" else fixed + rest
    assert len(demos) == K
    return demos


def main():
    tasks = load_tasks()
    out = []
    for t, (train, test, spec) in tasks.items():
        n_labels = len(spec["labels"])
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_of("test", t))
        per = N_TEST_PER_TASK // n_labels
        test_idx = np.concatenate([rng.choice(np.where(test.label.values == l)[0], per, replace=False)
                                   for l in range(n_labels)])
        pools = {}
        for l in range(n_labels):
            ids = np.where(train.label.values == l)[0]
            nw = train.nwords.values[ids]
            q1, q2 = np.quantile(nw, [1 / 3, 2 / 3])
            pools[l] = dict(all=ids, short=ids[nw <= q1], long=ids[nw >= q2])
        print(t, "train pool", len(train), "test", len(test_idx),
              {l: (len(p["short"]), len(p["long"])) for l, p in pools.items()})
        for ti in test_idx:
            row = test.iloc[ti]
            for T in range(n_labels):
                for cond in CONDITIONS:
                    r = np.random.default_rng(seed_of(t, ti, T, cond))
                    demos = build_demos(train, spec, T, cond, r, pools)
                    prompt = spec["instr"] + "\n\n" + "".join(fmt_example(d, spec) for d in demos) \
                        + fmt_example(row, spec, with_label=False)
                    out.append(dict(
                        task=t, test_id=int(ti), gold=int(row.label), T=T, cond=cond,
                        test_nwords=int(row.nwords), labels=spec["labels"],
                        demo_labels=[int(d.label) for d in demos],
                        demo_nwords=[int(d.nwords) for d in demos], prompt=prompt))
    path = f"{ROOT}/datasets/prompts/prompts.jsonl"
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        for o in out:
            f.write(json.dumps(o) + "\n")
    print("wrote", len(out), "prompts ->", path)
    df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    print(df.groupby(["task", "cond"]).size().unstack())
    df["frac_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["last2_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d[-2:]) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["first2_T"] = [np.mean(np.array(d[:2]) == T) for d, T in zip(df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["lenT_minus_other"] = [np.mean([w for w, l in zip(nw, d) if l == T]) - np.mean([w for w, l in zip(nw, d) if l != T])
                              for nw, d, T in zip(df.demo_nwords, df.demo_labels, df["T"])]
    df["plen"] = df.prompt.str.split().str.len()
    print(df.groupby(["task", "cond"])[["frac_T", "first2_T", "last2_T", "lenT_minus_other", "plen"]].mean().round(2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

For each prompt we take the next-token distribution restricted to the label
words' first tokens (leading space), renormalised over the label set
(logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs" + allowed_token_ids).  Greedy prediction
= argmax of that distribution.  Output: results/raw/<tag>.jsonl with the

usage: python src/run_model.py <hf_model_id> <tag> [gpu_mem_gb]
"""
import os, sys, json, math, time
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
import torch
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def main():
    model, tag = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    want_gb = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
    out_path = f"{ROOT}/results/raw/{tag}.jsonl"
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(f"{ROOT}/datasets/prompts/prompts.jsonl")]
    free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
    budget = (want_gb * 1e9) if want_gb else free - 1.5e9
    budget = min(budget, free - 1.2e9)
    util = budget / total
    print(f"[{tag}] free={free/1e9:.1f}GB util={util:.3f}", flush=True)
    small = budget < 12e9
    llm = LLM(model=model, gpu_memory_utilization=util, max_model_len=3072,
              enable_prefix_caching=True, enforce_eager=small, seed=0,
              max_num_seqs=32 if small else 128,
              max_num_batched_tokens=2048 if small else 8192,
              logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs")
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
    t0 = time.time()
    with open(out_path + ".partial", "w") as f:
        for task in sorted({r["task"] for r in rows}):
            sub = [r for r in rows if r["task"] == task]
            labels = sub[0]["labels"]
            ids = [tok.encode(" " + w, add_special_tokens=False) for w in labels]
            assert all(len(i) >= 1 for i in ids)
            first = [i[0] for i in ids]
            assert len(set(first)) == len(first), (task, ids)
            sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0.0, logprobs=len(labels),
                                allowed_token_ids=first)
            outs = llm.generate([r["prompt"] for r in sub], sp, use_tqdm=False)
            for r, o in zip(sub, outs):
                lp = o.outputs[0].logprobs[0]
                logp = [lp[i].logprob if i in lp else -math.inf for i in first]
                m = max(logp); p = [math.exp(x - m) for x in logp]; s = sum(p)
                p = [x / s for x in p]
                f.write(json.dumps(dict(task=task, test_id=r["test_id"], T=r["T"], cond=r["cond"],
                                        gold=r["gold"], test_nwords=r["test_nwords"], probs=p)) + "\n")
            print(f"[{tag}] {task} done {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    os.replace(out_path + ".partial", out_path)
    print(f"[{tag}] DONE {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Planning: In-Context Learning Label Bias

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Few-shot prompting is the default way practitioners adapt LLMs to classification, and the demonstrations are often picked ad hoc. If superficial demonstration statistics (label counts, order, length) move predictions, a deployed classifier can quietly change behaviour depending on which examples were pasted into the prompt. Knowing how large each bias is, and whether it shrinks with scale, tells practitioners which properties of a demonstration set they actually need to control.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this workspace: papers/, datasets/ and code/ were missing. The background below comes from known work.) Zhao et al. (2021, *Calibrate Before Use*) documented majority-label, recency and common-token bias in GPT-3, mostly with small numbers of prompts on one model family, and proposed contextual calibration. Fei et al. (2023) added "domain-label bias" and domain-context calibration. Min et al. (2022) showed that label correctness matters less than format. Lu et al. (2022) showed that order sensitivity is large. Most of these studies vary one factor at a time on older GPT-3-era models. None (a) measure frequency, recency, position *and* length-label correlation side by side with the same protocol, (b) do so across a dense scale ladder (0.5B to 14B) of a single modern instruction-tuned family, or (c) report calibration and entropy for each bias type.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled, fully paired benchmark of four demonstration manipulations (frequency skew, recency, primacy/label-position, label-length correlation) against a clean baseline on 4 NLU tasks and 5 model sizes. The manipulation's target label is rotated through every label, so a model's intrinsic label prior cancels out and the "shift toward the target label" can be read directly. We report accuracy, calibration (ECE) and entropy.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (bias magnitude by type): estimates the shift toward the target label for each manipulation. This tests the claimed ordering skew > recency > length.
- Exp 2 (scale ladder 0.5B→14B): tests "larger models correct skew but amplify recency" and "length bias is hard to overcome with scale".
- Exp 3 (calibration/entropy): tests "ECE increases monotonically with all bias types".
- Exp 4 (length interaction): checks whether the length manipulation teaches a length→label *rule* (long test inputs pushed toward T) rather than a blanket prior shift.

## Research Question
How much does each type of spurious demonstration statistic shift an LLM's few-shot predictions toward the favoured label, and how does this depend on model scale? Types: label frequency, recency, label position (primacy), and label-length correlation.

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: skew produces a 15–25 pp shift toward the majority label, the largest of all types.
- H2: recency produces an 8–15 pp shift, second largest.
- H3: length correlation produces a 5–10 pp shift that does not shrink with scale.
- H4: the skew shift decreases with scale, and the recency shift increases with scale.
- H5: ECE(cond) > ECE(clean) for every bias type.

## Proposed Methodology
### Approach
- Models: local Qwen2.5-Instruct models at 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B and 14B, run in vLLM. No API keys are available on this host and the idea specifies local models. vLLM is used instead of Ollama because it gives exact label log-probs.
- Prompts are raw completion-style text with a one-line task instruction and k=10 demonstrations.
- Prediction is the argmax of the next-token distribution restricted to the label words and renormalised over them. This avoids parsing failures and gives probabilities for calibration.
- Tasks:
  - SST-2 (sentiment, 2-way)
  - RTE (NLI, 2-way)
  - AG News (topic, 4-way)
  - MRPC (paraphrase, 2-way)
- Each task has 200 gold-balanced test items from the validation/test split. Demos are drawn from the train split.

### Conditions (k = 10, target label T rotated over all labels)
| cond | label counts | order | lengths |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean | balanced (5/5; 3/3/2/2) | random | random |
| skew | 8 T / 2 other | random | random |
| recency | balanced | last 2 = T | random |
| primacy (label-position) | balanced | first 2 = T | random |
| length | balanced | random | T demos from longest third, others from shortest third |

"Label-position correlation (label always near sentence start)" is interpreted at the *prompt* level: T demonstrations occupy the first positions (primacy). This is the counterpart of recency. The deviation is documented.

There are 10,000 prompts per model (4 tasks × 200 items × |L| targets × 5 conditions). The same prompts are used for all models, so comparisons are paired.

### Baselines
The clean balanced demonstration set, with its own fresh sample per (item, T). The no-bias reference rates are P(pred=T | clean), which equals 1/|L| on average.

### Evaluation Metrics
- Target shift Δ = P(pred=T | cond) − P(pred=T | clean), in percentage points. This is the primary bias measure.
- Accuracy and the accuracy drop relative to clean.
- ECE (10 equal-width bins, max-prob confidence).
- Mean predictive entropy (normalised by log|L|).
- Mean probability mass on T (a soft version of Δ).
- For the length condition: Δ on long test inputs (above the median) vs short ones.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- 95% CIs come from a cluster bootstrap over test items (2,000 resamples).

# Planning: In-Context Learning Label Bias

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Few-shot prompting is the default way practitioners adapt LLMs to classification, and the demonstrations are often picked ad hoc. If superficial demonstration statistics (label counts, order, length) move predictions, a deployed classifier can quietly change behaviour depending on which examples were pasted into the prompt. Knowing how large each bias is, and whether it shrinks with scale, tells practitioners which properties of a demonstration set they actually need to control.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this workspace: papers/, datasets/ and code/ were missing. The background below comes from known work.) Zhao et al. (2021, *Calibrate Before Use*) documented majority-label, recency and common-token bias in GPT-3, mostly with small numbers of prompts on one model family, and proposed contextual calibration. Fei et al. (2023) added "domain-label bias" and domain-context calibration. Min et al. (2022) showed that label correctness matters less than format. Lu et al. (2022) showed that order sensitivity is large. Most of these studies vary one factor at a time on older GPT-3-era models. None (a) measure frequency, recency, position *and* length-label correlation side by side with the same protocol, (b) do so across a dense scale ladder (0.5B to 14B) of a single modern instruction-tuned family, or (c) report calibration and entropy for each bias type.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled, fully paired benchmark of four demonstration manipulations (frequency skew, recency, primacy/label-position, label-length correlation) against a clean baseline on 4 NLU tasks and 5 model sizes. The manipulation's target label is rotated through every label, so a model's intrinsic label prior cancels out and the "shift toward the target label" can be read directly. We report accuracy, calibration (ECE) and entropy.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (bias magnitude by type): estimates the shift toward the target label for each manipulation. This tests the claimed ordering skew > recency > length.
- Exp 2 (scale ladder 0.5B→14B): tests "larger models correct skew but amplify recency" and "length bias is hard to overcome with scale".
- Exp 3 (calibration/entropy): tests "ECE increases monotonically with all bias types".
- Exp 4 (length interaction): checks whether the length manipulation teaches a length→label *rule* (long test inputs pushed toward T) rather than a blanket prior shift.

## Research Question
How much does each type of spurious demonstration statistic shift an LLM's few-shot predictions toward the favoured label, and how does this depend on model scale? Types: label frequency, recency, label position (primacy), and label-length correlation.

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: skew produces a 15–25 pp shift toward the majority label, the largest of all types.
- H2: recency produces an 8–15 pp shift, second largest.
- H3: length correlation produces a 5–10 pp shift that does not shrink with scale.
- H4: the skew shift decreases with scale, and the recency shift increases with scale.
- H5: ECE(cond) > ECE(clean) for every bias type.

## Proposed Methodology
### Approach
- Models: local Qwen2.5-Instruct models at 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B and 14B, run in vLLM. No API keys are available on this host and the idea specifies local models. vLLM is used instead of Ollama because it gives exact label log-probs.
- Prompts are raw completion-style text with a one-line task instruction and k=10 demonstrations.
- Prediction is the argmax of the next-token distribution restricted to the label words and renormalised over them. This avoids parsing failures and gives probabilities for calibration.
- Tasks:
  - SST-2 (sentiment, 2-way)
  - RTE (NLI, 2-way)
  - AG News (topic, 4-way)
  - MRPC (paraphrase, 2-way)
- Each task has 200 gold-balanced test items from the validation/test split. Demos are drawn from the train split.

### Conditions (k = 10, target label T rotated over all labels)
| cond | label counts | order | lengths |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean | balanced (5/5; 3/3/2/2) | random | random |
| skew | 8 T / 2 other | random | random |
| recency | balanced | last 2 = T | random |
| primacy (label-position) | balanced | first 2 = T | random |
| length | balanced | random | T demos from longest third, others from shortest third |

"Label-position correlation (label always near sentence start)" is interpreted at the *prompt* level: T demonstrations occupy the first positions (primacy). This is the counterpart of recency. The deviation is documented.

There are 10,000 prompts per model (4 tasks × 200 items × |L| targets × 5 conditions). The same prompts are used for all models, so comparisons are paired.

The clean balanced demonstration set, with its own fresh sample per (item, T). The no-bias reference rates are P(pred=T | clean), which equals 1/|L| on average.

- Target shift Δ = P(pred=T | cond) − P(pred=T | clean), in percentage points. This is the primary bias measure.
- Accuracy and the accuracy drop relative to clean.
- ECE (10 equal-width bins, max-prob confidence).
- Mean predictive entropy (normalised by log|L|).
- Mean probability mass on T (a soft version of Δ).
- For the length condition: Δ on long test inputs (above the median) vs short ones.

- Paired sign-flip permutation tests on the per-item Δ, with Holm correction across conditions × models.
- Scale trend: OLS slope of Δ on log10(params), with a CI from bootstrapping over items.
- Calibration: the ECE difference from clean, with a bootstrap CI.

## Expected Outcomes
H1 is supported if Δ_skew lies in [15, 25] and exceeds every other Δ. H4 is supported if the skew slope is negative and the recency slope is positive (CI excluding 0). H5 is supported if ECE(cond) − ECE(clean) > 0 for all conditions in most models.

- Model runs: about 2–3 h, constrained by the shared GPUs.
- Analysis: 45 min.
- Report: 45 min.

## Potential Challenges

- Ceiling effects on SST-2/AG News for large models would compress shifts. We report per-task results.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: gpu_run.sh <min_free_MiB> <model> <tag> [gpu_mem_gb]
# Waits until some GPU has >= min_free MiB free, launches run_model.py there,
# retries on failure (waiting does not count as a try). Writes logs/<tag>.status.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
export HF_HOME=/data/transformers HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
min=$1; model=$2; tag=$3; gb=$4; tries=0
[ -f results/raw/$tag.jsonl ] && { echo DONE > logs/$tag.status; exit 0; }
while [ $tries -lt 8 ]; do
  gpu=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | sort -t, -k2 -nr | awk -F', ' -v m=$min '$2>=m{print $1; exit}')
  if [ -z "$gpu" ]; then echo "WAIT $(date +%T)" > logs/$tag.status; sleep 30; continue; fi
  echo "RUN gpu$gpu try$tries $(date +%T)" > logs/$tag.status
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpu python src/run_model.py $model $tag $gb >> logs/$tag.log 2>&1
  if [ -f results/raw/$tag.jsonl ]; then echo DONE > logs/$tag.status; exit 0; fi
  tries=$((tries+1)); sleep 30
done
echo FAILED > logs/$tag.status
EOF
chmod +x src/gpu_run.sh

cat > /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/icl_label_bias_20261020_001001_e5f6g7h8/src/analyze.py <<'EOF'
"""Analysis of ICL label-bias runs: shifts, accuracy, calibration, stats, figures.

Primary metric: target shift  Δ = P(pred = T | cond) − P(pred = T | clean),
paired on (task, test item, target label T).  Δ is averaged over T and items
within a task, then tasks are weighted equally.  CIs: cluster bootstrap over
test items (resampled within task).  Significance: sign-flip permutation test
on per-item Δ, Holm-corrected over all (model, condition) tests.
"""
import os, json, glob
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
RES, FIG = f"{ROOT}/results", f"{ROOT}/figures"
B = 2000
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
CONDS = ["skew", "recency", "primacy", "length"]
MODELS = [  # tag, label, params (B), family
    ("qwen0.5b", "Qwen2.5-0.5B", 0.5, "qwen"), ("qwen1.5b", "Qwen2.5-1.5B", 1.5, "qwen"),
    ("qwen3b", "Qwen2.5-3B", 3, "qwen"), ("qwen7b", "Qwen2.5-7B", 7, "qwen"),
    ("qwen14b", "Qwen2.5-14B", 14, "qwen"), ("llama1b", "Llama-3.2-1B", 1.2, "llama"),
    ("llama8b", "Llama-3.1-8B", 8, "llama")]
TASKS = ["sst2", "rte", "agnews", "mrpc"]


def load():
    dfs = []
    for tag, name, size, fam in MODELS:
        p = f"{RES}/raw/{tag}.jsonl"
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        d = pd.read_json(p, lines=True)
        d["model"], d["size"], d["family"] = name, size, fam
        dfs.append(d)
    d = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
    P = np.stack(d.probs.apply(lambda x: np.pad(x, (0, 4 - len(x)))).values)
    d["nl"] = d.probs.apply(len)
    d["pred"] = P.argmax(1)
    d["conf"] = P.max(1)
    d["acc"] = (d.pred == d.gold).astype(float)
    d["predT"] = (d.pred == d["T"]).astype(float)
    d["pT"] = P[np.arange(len(d)), d["T"].values]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ent = -np.nansum(np.where(P > 0, P * np.log(P), 0), 1)
    d["entropy"] = ent / np.log(d.nl)
    med = d.groupby("task").test_nwords.transform("median")
    d["long_test"] = d.test_nwords > med
    return d


def ece(conf, correct, nb=10):
    bins = np.minimum((conf * nb).astype(int), nb - 1)
    e = 0.0
    for b in range(nb):
        m = bins == b
        if m.any():
            e += m.mean() * abs(correct[m].mean() - conf[m].mean())
    return e


def item_deltas(d, metric="predT"):
    """Per (model, task, test_id, cond) Δ averaged over T, relative to clean."""
    k = ["model", "task", "test_id", "T"]
    w = d.pivot_table(index=k, columns="cond", values=metric).reset_index()
    for c in CONDS:
        w[c] = w[c] - w["clean"]
    return w.groupby(["model", "task", "test_id"])[CONDS].mean().reset_index()


def boot_task_mean(item_df, col, B=B):
    """Equal-task-weighted mean with cluster bootstrap over items within task."""
    groups = [g[col].values for _, g in item_df.groupby("task")]
    point = np.mean([g.mean() for g in groups])
    bs = np.zeros(B)
    for b in range(B):
        bs[b] = np.mean([g[rng.integers(0, len(g), len(g))].mean() for g in groups])
    return point, np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5), bs


def signflip_p(x, n=10000):
    x = np.asarray(x); obs = abs(x.mean())
    s = rng.choice([-1, 1], size=(n, len(x)))
    return (np.sum(np.abs((s * x).mean(1)) >= obs) + 1) / (n + 1)


def holm(ps):
    ps = np.asarray(ps); o = np.argsort(ps); m = len(ps); adj = np.empty(m); run = 0
    for r, i in enumerate(o):
        run = max(run, (m - r) * ps[i]); adj[i] = min(1, run)
    return adj


def main():
    d = load()
    models = [m[1] for m in MODELS if m[1] in d.model.unique()]
    sizes = {m[1]: m[2] for m in MODELS}
    print("models:", models, "rows:", len(d))
    summary = {}

    # ---------- per-condition descriptive table (per task + pooled) ----------
    rows = []
    for (m, t, c), g in d.groupby(["model", "task", "cond"]):
        rows.append(dict(model=m, task=t, cond=c, acc=g.acc.mean(), predT=g.predT.mean(),
                         pT=g.pT.mean(), ece=ece(g.conf.values, g.acc.values),
                         entropy=g.entropy.mean(), conf=g.conf.mean()))
    desc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    desc.to_csv(f"{RES}/per_task_condition_metrics.csv", index=False)

    # ---------- Δ (target shift) with CIs + tests ----------
    itm = item_deltas(d, "predT")
    itm_soft = item_deltas(d, "pT")
    itm_acc = item_deltas(d, "acc")
    shift_rows, pvals = [], []
    boots = {}
    for m in models:
        for c in CONDS:
            sub = itm[itm.model == m]
            pt, lo, hi, bs = boot_task_mean(sub, c)
            boots[(m, c)] = bs
            # per-item mean over tasks for sign-flip: center tasks equally by using all items
            p = signflip_p(sub[c].values)
            ps, _, _, _ = boot_task_mean(itm_soft[itm_soft.model == m], c, B=1)
            pa, alo, ahi, _ = boot_task_mean(itm_acc[itm_acc.model == m], c)
            per_task = sub.groupby("task")[c].mean().to_dict()
            shift_rows.append(dict(model=m, size=sizes[m], cond=c, delta_pp=100 * pt,
                                   lo=100 * lo, hi=100 * hi, soft_delta_pp=100 * ps,
                                   dacc_pp=100 * pa, dacc_lo=100 * alo, dacc_hi=100 * ahi, p=p,
                                   **{f"delta_{t}": 100 * per_task.get(t, np.nan) for t in TASKS}))
            pvals.append(p)
    shifts = pd.DataFrame(shift_rows)
    shifts["p_holm"] = holm(shifts.p.values)
    shifts.to_csv(f"{RES}/target_shift.csv", index=False)
    print("\n=== Target shift Δ (pp) toward manipulated label, equal-task mean ===")
    print(shifts[["model", "cond", "delta_pp", "lo", "hi", "soft_delta_pp", "dacc_pp", "p_holm"]
                 + [f"delta_{t}" for t in TASKS]].round(2).to_string(index=False))

    # ranking of conditions per model
    rank = shifts.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="delta_pp").loc[models]
    print("\nΔ pivot (pp):\n", rank.round(1))

    # ---------- skew decomposition: gold==T vs gold!=T ----------
    k = ["model", "task", "test_id", "T"]
    w = d.pivot_table(index=k + ["gold"], columns="cond", values="acc").reset_index()
    w["is_T"] = w.gold == w["T"]
    dec = w.groupby(["model", "is_T"])[["clean", "skew", "recency", "length"]].mean().unstack().round(3)
    print("\nAccuracy split by gold==T:\n", dec)
    dec.to_csv(f"{RES}/acc_by_gold_is_T.csv")

    # ---------- scale slopes (Qwen ladder) ----------
    qwen = [m for m in models if m.startswith("Qwen")]
    slope_rows = []
    if len(qwen) >= 3:
        x = np.log10([sizes[m] for m in qwen])
        for c in CONDS:
            y = shifts.set_index(["model", "cond"]).loc[[(m, c) for m in qwen], "delta_pp"].values
            sl = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0]
            bs = np.array([np.polyfit(x, 100 * np.array([boots[(m, c)][b] for m in qwen]), 1)[0]
                           for b in range(B)])
            # bootstraps are independent per model (not perfectly paired); conservative CI
            slope_rows.append(dict(cond=c, slope_pp_per_decade=sl, lo=np.percentile(bs, 2.5),
                                   hi=np.percentile(bs, 97.5),
                                   spearman_rho=pd.Series(y).corr(pd.Series(x), method="spearman")))
        slopes = pd.DataFrame(slope_rows)
        slopes.to_csv(f"{RES}/scale_slopes.csv", index=False)
        print("\nScale slopes (Qwen, pp per 10x params):\n", slopes.round(2))

    # ---------- calibration ----------
    cal_rows = []
    for m in models:
        for c in ["clean"] + CONDS:
            per = desc[(desc.model == m) & (desc.cond == c)]
            cal_rows.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, ece=per.ece.mean(), acc=per.acc.mean(),
                                 entropy=per.entropy.mean(), conf=per.conf.mean()))
    cal = pd.DataFrame(cal_rows)
    # bootstrap CI on ECE(cond)-ECE(clean), resampling items within task (paired)
    dci = []
    for m in models:
        gm = d[d.model == m]
        tasks = {t: gm[gm.task == t] for t in TASKS}
        ids = {t: g.test_id.unique() for t, g in tasks.items()}
        bucket = {(t, c): {i: g2 for i, g2 in g[g.cond == c].groupby("test_id")} for t, g in tasks.items()
                  for c in ["clean"] + CONDS}
        for c in CONDS:
            diffs = []
            for b in range(300):
                vals = []
                for t in TASKS:
                    s = rng.choice(ids[t], len(ids[t]))
                    gc = pd.concat([bucket[(t, "clean")][i] for i in s])
                    gx = pd.concat([bucket[(t, c)][i] for i in s])
                    vals.append(ece(gx.conf.values, gx.acc.values) - ece(gc.conf.values, gc.acc.values))
                diffs.append(np.mean(vals))
            pt = cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == c)].ece.item() - cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == "clean")].ece.item()
            dci.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, dECE=pt, lo=np.percentile(diffs, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(diffs, 97.5)))
    dci = pd.DataFrame(dci)
    cal.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration.csv", index=False)
    dci.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration_delta.csv", index=False)
    print("\nCalibration (equal-task mean):\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="ece").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nΔECE vs clean with CI:\n", dci.round(3).to_string(index=False))
    print("\nEntropy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="entropy").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nAccuracy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="acc").loc[models].round(3))

    # ---------- length interaction ----------
    w = d.pivot_table(index=["model", "task", "test_id", "T", "long_test"], columns="cond", values="predT").reset_index()
    w["dlen"] = w["length"] - w["clean"]
    li = w.groupby(["model", "long_test"]).dlen.mean().unstack() * 100
    li.columns = ["short_test", "long_test"]
    li["long_minus_short"] = li.long_test - li.short_test
    # bootstrap CI for long-minus-short
    lis = []
    for m in models:
        g = w[w.model == m]
        it = g.groupby(["task", "test_id", "long_test"]).dlen.mean().reset_index()
        L, S = it[it.long_test].dlen.values, it[~it.long_test].dlen.values
        bs = [L[rng.integers(0, len(L), len(L))].mean() - S[rng.integers(0, len(S), len(S))].mean() for _ in range(B)]
        lis.append((np.percentile(bs, 2.5) * 100, np.percentile(bs, 97.5) * 100))
    li = li.loc[models]
    li["lo"], li["hi"] = [a for a, _ in lis], [b for _, b in lis]
    li.to_csv(f"{RES}/length_interaction.csv")
    print("\nLength-condition Δ by test length (pp):\n", li.round(2))

    # ---------- figures ----------
    colors = {"skew": "#3b6fb6", "recency": "#d9822b", "primacy": "#5aa36c", "length": "#a35aa3"}
    # Fig 1: Δ by condition × model
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.2))
    n = len(CONDS); wdt = 0.8 / n
    for j, c in enumerate(CONDS):
        s = shifts[shifts.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        xs = np.arange(len(models)) + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * wdt
        ax.bar(xs, s.delta_pp, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c,
               yerr=[s.delta_pp - s.lo, s.hi - s.delta_pp], capsize=2, error_kw=dict(lw=0.8))
    ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6)
    ax.axhspan(15, 25, color=colors["skew"], alpha=0.08)
    ax.axhspan(8, 15, color=colors["recency"], alpha=0.08)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(models))); ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=15)
    ax.set_ylabel("Δ P(pred = target) vs clean (pp)")
    ax.set_title("Shift toward the manipulated label (mean of 4 tasks, 95% bootstrap CI)\n"
                 "shaded: hypothesised ranges (skew 15–25, recency 8–15)")
    ax.legend(ncol=4, frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig1_target_shift.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: scale curves per task (Qwen)
    if len(qwen) >= 2:
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 5, figsize=(16, 3.4), sharey=True)
        xs = [sizes[m] for m in qwen]
        for ax, t in zip(axes, ["mean"] + TASKS):
            for c in CONDS:
                s = shifts[shifts.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[qwen]
                y = s.delta_pp if t == "mean" else s[f"delta_{t}"]
                ax.plot(xs, y, "o-", color=colors[c], label=c)
                if t == "mean":
                    ax.fill_between(xs, s.lo, s.hi, color=colors[c], alpha=0.12)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
            ax.set_title("4-task mean" if t == "mean" else t); ax.set_xlabel("params (B)")
        axes[0].set_ylabel("Δ target rate (pp)"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
        fig.suptitle("Bias vs. model scale (Qwen2.5-Instruct ladder)", y=1.02)
        fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig2_scale.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: ΔECE and accuracy
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3.8))
    for j, c in enumerate(CONDS):
        s = dci[dci.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        xs = np.arange(len(models)) + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * wdt
        axes[0].bar(xs, 100 * s.dECE, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c,
                    yerr=[100 * (s.dECE - s.lo), 100 * (s.hi - s.dECE)], capsize=2, error_kw=dict(lw=0.8))
        a = cal[cal.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values - cal[cal.cond == "clean"].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values
        axes[1].bar(xs, 100 * a, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c)

    d["pred"] = P.argmax(1)
    d["conf"] = P.max(1)

    d["predT"] = (d.pred == d["T"]).astype(float)

    bins = np.minimum((conf * nb).astype(int), nb - 1)
    e = 0.0
    for b in range(nb):
        m = bins == b
        if m.any():
            e += m.mean() * abs(correct[m].mean() - conf[m].mean())
    return e

    """Per (model, task, test_id, cond) Δ averaged over T, relative to clean."""
    k = ["model", "task", "test_id", "T"]

    groups = [g[col].values for _, g in item_df.groupby("task")]

    bs = np.zeros(B)
    for b in range(B):
        bs[b] = np.mean([g[rng.integers(0, len(g), len(g))].mean() for g in groups])
    return point, np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5), bs

    return adj

                s = shifts[shifts.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[qwen]
                y = s.delta_pp if t == "mean" else s[f"delta_{t}"]
                ax.plot(xs, y, "o-", color=colors[c], label=c)
                if t == "mean":
                    ax.fill_between(xs, s.lo, s.hi, color=colors[c], alpha=0.12)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
            ax.set_title("4-task mean" if t == "mean" else t); ax.set_xlabel("params (B)")
        axes[0].set_ylabel("Δ target rate (pp)"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)

        fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig2_scale.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: ΔECE and accuracy
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3.8))
    for j, c in enumerate(CONDS):
        s = dci[dci.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        xs = np.arange(len(models)) + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * wdt
        axes[0].bar(xs, 100 * s.dECE, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c,
                    yerr=[100 * (s.dECE - s.lo), 100 * (s.hi - s.dECE)], capsize=2, error_kw=dict(lw=0.8))
        a = cal[cal.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values - cal[cal.cond == "clean"].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values
        axes[1].bar(xs, 100 * a, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c)
    for ax, yl in zip(axes, ["ΔECE vs clean (pp)", "Δ accuracy vs clean (pp)"]):
        ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6); ax.set_xticks(range(len(models)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=20, fontsize=8); ax.set_ylabel(yl)
    axes[0].legend(ncol=2, frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[0].set_title("Calibration error change"); axes[1].set_title("Accuracy change")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig3_calibration_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)
    print("figures written")

#!/bin/bash
# usage: gpu_run.sh <min_free_MiB> <model> <tag> [gpu_mem_gb]
# Waits until some GPU has >= min_free MiB free, launches run_model.py there,
# retries on failure (waiting does not count as a try). Writes logs/<tag>.status.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
export HF_HOME=/data/transformers HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
min=$1; model=$2; tag=$3; gb=$4; tries=0
sfx=""; [ "$PROMPTS" = "prompts_supp" ] && sfx="__supp"
[ -f results/raw/$tag$sfx.jsonl ] && { echo DONE > logs/$tag$sfx.status; exit 0; }
while [ $tries -lt 8 ]; do
  gpu=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | sort -t, -k2 -nr | awk -F', ' -v m=$min '$2>=m{print $1; exit}')
  if [ -z "$gpu" ]; then echo "WAIT $(date +%T)" > logs/$tag$sfx.status; sleep 30; continue; fi
  echo "RUN gpu$gpu try$tries $(date +%T)" > logs/$tag$sfx.status
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpu python src/run_model.py $model $tag $gb >> logs/$tag$sfx.log 2>&1
  if [ -f results/raw/$tag$sfx.jsonl ]; then echo DONE > logs/$tag$sfx.status; exit 0; fi
  tries=$((tries+1)); sleep 30
done
echo FAILED > logs/$tag$sfx.status

"""Dose-response analysis: skew 60/80/100% and recency last-2 vs last-4,
each paired with the main run's clean prompt for the same (task, item, T)."""
import os, numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from analyze import MODELS, RES, FIG, TASKS, load, boot_task_mean

def main():
    d = load()
    rows = []
    for tag, name, size, fam in MODELS:
        p = f"{RES}/raw/{tag}__supp.jsonl"
        if not os.path.exists(p) or name not in d.model.unique():
            continue
        s = pd.read_json(p, lines=True)
        s["pred"] = s.probs.apply(np.argmax); s["predT"] = (s.pred == s["T"]).astype(float)
        main_ = d[d.model == name][["task", "test_id", "T", "cond", "predT"]]
        allc = pd.concat([main_, s[["task", "test_id", "T", "cond", "predT"]]])
        w = allc.pivot_table(index=["task", "test_id", "T"], columns="cond", values="predT").reset_index()
        for c in ["skew60", "skew", "skew100", "recency", "recency4"]:
            w[c + "_d"] = w[c] - w["clean"]
            it = w.groupby(["task", "test_id"])[c + "_d"].mean().reset_index()
            pt, lo, hi, _ = boot_task_mean(it, c + "_d")
            per = it.groupby("task")[c + "_d"].mean()
            rows.append(dict(model=name, cond=c, delta_pp=100 * pt, lo=100 * lo, hi=100 * hi,
                             **{f"delta_{t}": 100 * per[t] for t in TASKS}))
    r = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    r.to_csv(f"{RES}/dose_response.csv", index=False)
    print(r.round(1).to_string(index=False))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6))
    for m, g in r.groupby("model", sort=False):
        g = g.set_index("cond")
        sk = g.loc[["skew60", "skew", "skew100"]]
        ax[0].errorbar([60, 80, 100], sk.delta_pp, yerr=[sk.delta_pp - sk.lo, sk.hi - sk.delta_pp], marker="o", capsize=3, label=m)
        rc = g.loc[["recency", "recency4"]]
        ax[1].errorbar([2, 4], rc.delta_pp, yerr=[rc.delta_pp - rc.lo, rc.hi - rc.delta_pp], marker="o", capsize=3, label=m)
    ax[0].set_xlabel("% of demos with target label"); ax[1].set_xlabel("# final demos with target label")
    ax[1].set_xticks([2, 4])
    for a in ax: a.axhline(0, color="k", lw=.5); a.set_ylabel("Δ target rate vs clean (pp)")
    ax[0].set_title("Frequency-skew dose-response"); ax[1].set_title("Recency dose-response")
    ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig4_dose_response.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

"""Dose-response analysis: skew 60/80/100% and recency last-2 vs last-4,

import os, numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from analyze import MODELS, RES, FIG, TASKS, load, boot_task_mean

def main():
    d = load()
    rows = []
    for tag, name, size, fam in MODELS:
        p = f"{RES}/raw/{tag}__supp.jsonl"
        if not os.path.exists(p) or name not in d.model.unique():
            continue
        s = pd.read_json(p, lines=True)
        s["pred"] = s.probs.apply(np.argmax); s["predT"] = (s.pred == s["T"]).astype(float)
        main_ = d[d.model == name][["task", "test_id", "T", "cond", "predT"]]
        allc = pd.concat([main_, s[["task", "test_id", "T", "cond", "predT"]]])
        w = allc.pivot_table(index=["task", "test_id", "T"], columns="cond", values="predT").reset_index()
        for c in ["skew60", "skew", "skew100", "recency", "recency4"]:
            w[c + "_d"] = w[c] - w["clean"]
            it = w.groupby(["task", "test_id"])[c + "_d"].mean().reset_index()
            pt, lo, hi, _ = boot_task_mean(it, c + "_d")
            per = it.groupby("task")[c + "_d"].mean()
            rows.append(dict(model=name, cond=c, delta_pp=100 * pt, lo=100 * lo, hi=100 * hi,
                             **{f"delta_{t}": 100 * per[t] for t in TASKS}))
    r = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    r.to_csv(f"{RES}/dose_response.csv", index=False)
    print(r.round(1).to_string(index=False))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6))
    for m, g in r.groupby("model", sort=False):

        ax[0].errorbar([60, 80, 100], sk.delta_pp, yerr=[sk.delta_pp - sk.lo, sk.hi - sk.delta_pp], marker="o", capsize=3, label=m)
        rc = g.loc[["recency", "recency4"]]
        ax[1].errorbar([2, 4], rc.delta_pp, yerr=[rc.delta_pp - rc.lo, rc.hi - rc.delta_pp], marker="o", capsize=3, label=m)
    ax[0].set_xlabel("% of demos with target label"); ax[1].set_xlabel("# final demos with target label")
    ax[1].set_xticks([2, 4])
    for a in ax: a.axhline(0, color="k", lw=.5); a.set_ylabel("Δ target rate vs clean (pp)")
    ax[0].set_title("Frequency-skew dose-response"); ax[1].set_title("Recency dose-response")
    ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig4_dose_response.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Analysis of ICL label-bias runs: shifts, accuracy, calibration, stats, figures.

Primary metric: target shift  Δ = P(pred = T | cond) − P(pred = T | clean),
paired on (task, test item, target label T).  Δ is averaged over T and items
within a task, then tasks are weighted equally.  CIs: cluster bootstrap over
test items (resampled within task).  Significance: sign-flip permutation test
on per-item Δ, Holm-corrected over all (model, condition) tests.
"""
import os, json, glob
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
RES, FIG = f"{ROOT}/results", f"{ROOT}/figures"
B = 2000
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
CONDS = ["skew", "recency", "primacy", "length"]
MODELS = [  # tag, label, params (B), family
    ("qwen0.5b", "Qwen2.5-0.5B", 0.5, "qwen"), ("qwen1.5b", "Qwen2.5-1.5B", 1.5, "qwen"),
    ("qwen3b", "Qwen2.5-3B", 3, "qwen"), ("qwen7b-awq", "Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ", 7, "qwen"),
    ("qwen14b", "Qwen2.5-14B", 14, "qwen"), ("qwen1.5b-base", "Qwen2.5-1.5B-base", 1.5, "qwen-base"), ("llama1b", "Llama-3.2-1B", 1.2, "llama"),
    ("llama8b-awq", "Llama-3.1-8B-AWQ", 8, "llama")]
TASKS = ["sst2", "rte", "agnews", "mrpc"]


def load():
    dfs = []
    for tag, name, size, fam in MODELS:
        p = f"{RES}/raw/{tag}.jsonl"
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        d = pd.read_json(p, lines=True)
        d["model"], d["size"], d["family"] = name, size, fam
        dfs.append(d)
    d = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
    P = np.stack(d.probs.apply(lambda x: np.pad(x, (0, 4 - len(x)))).values)
    d["nl"] = d.probs.apply(len)
    d["pred"] = P.argmax(1)
    d["conf"] = P.max(1)
    d["acc"] = (d.pred == d.gold).astype(float)
    d["predT"] = (d.pred == d["T"]).astype(float)
    d["pT"] = P[np.arange(len(d)), d["T"].values]
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ent = -np.nansum(np.where(P > 0, P * np.log(P), 0), 1)
    d["entropy"] = ent / np.log(d.nl)
    med = d.groupby("task").test_nwords.transform("median")
    d["long_test"] = d.test_nwords > med
    return d


def ece(conf, correct, nb=10):
    bins = np.minimum((conf * nb).astype(int), nb - 1)
    e = 0.0
    for b in range(nb):
        m = bins == b
        if m.any():
            e += m.mean() * abs(correct[m].mean() - conf[m].mean())
    return e


def item_deltas(d, metric="predT"):
    """Per (model, task, test_id, cond) Δ averaged over T, relative to clean."""
    k = ["model", "task", "test_id", "T"]
    w = d.pivot_table(index=k, columns="cond", values=metric).reset_index()
    for c in CONDS:
        w[c] = w[c] - w["clean"]
    return w.groupby(["model", "task", "test_id"])[CONDS].mean().reset_index()


def boot_task_mean(item_df, col, B=B):
    """Equal-task-weighted mean with cluster bootstrap over items within task."""
    groups = [g[col].values for _, g in item_df.groupby("task")]
    point = np.mean([g.mean() for g in groups])
    bs = np.zeros(B)
    for b in range(B):
        bs[b] = np.mean([g[rng.integers(0, len(g), len(g))].mean() for g in groups])
    return point, np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5), bs


def signflip_p(x, n=10000):
    x = np.asarray(x); obs = abs(x.mean())
    s = rng.choice([-1, 1], size=(n, len(x)))
    return (np.sum(np.abs((s * x).mean(1)) >= obs) + 1) / (n + 1)


def holm(ps):
    ps = np.asarray(ps); o = np.argsort(ps); m = len(ps); adj = np.empty(m); run = 0
    for r, i in enumerate(o):
        run = max(run, (m - r) * ps[i]); adj[i] = min(1, run)
    return adj


def main():
    d = load()
    models = [m[1] for m in MODELS if m[1] in d.model.unique()]
    sizes = {m[1]: m[2] for m in MODELS}
    print("models:", models, "rows:", len(d))
    summary = {}

    # ---------- per-condition descriptive table (per task + pooled) ----------
    rows = []
    for (m, t, c), g in d.groupby(["model", "task", "cond"]):
        rows.append(dict(model=m, task=t, cond=c, acc=g.acc.mean(), predT=g.predT.mean(),
                         pT=g.pT.mean(), ece=ece(g.conf.values, g.acc.values),
                         entropy=g.entropy.mean(), conf=g.conf.mean()))
    desc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    desc.to_csv(f"{RES}/per_task_condition_metrics.csv", index=False)

    # ---------- Δ (target shift) with CIs + tests ----------
    itm = item_deltas(d, "predT")
    itm_soft = item_deltas(d, "pT")
    itm_acc = item_deltas(d, "acc")
    shift_rows, pvals = [], []
    boots = {}
    for m in models:
        for c in CONDS:
            sub = itm[itm.model == m]
            pt, lo, hi, bs = boot_task_mean(sub, c)
            boots[(m, c)] = bs
            # per-item mean over tasks for sign-flip: center tasks equally by using all items
            p = signflip_p(sub[c].values)
            ps, _, _, _ = boot_task_mean(itm_soft[itm_soft.model == m], c, B=1)
            pa, alo, ahi, _ = boot_task_mean(itm_acc[itm_acc.model == m], c)
            per_task = sub.groupby("task")[c].mean().to_dict()
            shift_rows.append(dict(model=m, size=sizes[m], cond=c, delta_pp=100 * pt,
                                   lo=100 * lo, hi=100 * hi, soft_delta_pp=100 * ps,
                                   dacc_pp=100 * pa, dacc_lo=100 * alo, dacc_hi=100 * ahi, p=p,
                                   **{f"delta_{t}": 100 * per_task.get(t, np.nan) for t in TASKS}))
            pvals.append(p)
    shifts = pd.DataFrame(shift_rows)
    shifts["p_holm"] = holm(shifts.p.values)
    shifts.to_csv(f"{RES}/target_shift.csv", index=False)
    print("\n=== Target shift Δ (pp) toward manipulated label, equal-task mean ===")
    print(shifts[["model", "cond", "delta_pp", "lo", "hi", "soft_delta_pp", "dacc_pp", "p_holm"]
                 + [f"delta_{t}" for t in TASKS]].round(2).to_string(index=False))

    # ranking of conditions per model
    rank = shifts.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="delta_pp").loc[models]
    print("\nΔ pivot (pp):\n", rank.round(1))

    # ---------- skew decomposition: gold==T vs gold!=T ----------
    k = ["model", "task", "test_id", "T"]
    w = d.pivot_table(index=k + ["gold"], columns="cond", values="acc").reset_index()
    w["is_T"] = w.gold == w["T"]
    dec = w.groupby(["model", "is_T"])[["clean", "skew", "recency", "length"]].mean().unstack().round(3)
    print("\nAccuracy split by gold==T:\n", dec)
    dec.to_csv(f"{RES}/acc_by_gold_is_T.csv")

    # ---------- scale slopes (Qwen ladder) ----------
    qwen = [m for m in models if m.startswith("Qwen") and not m.endswith("base")]
    slope_rows = []
    if len(qwen) >= 3:
        x = np.log10([sizes[m] for m in qwen])
        for c in CONDS:
            y = shifts.set_index(["model", "cond"]).loc[[(m, c) for m in qwen], "delta_pp"].values
            sl = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0]
            bs = np.array([np.polyfit(x, 100 * np.array([boots[(m, c)][b] for m in qwen]), 1)[0]
                           for b in range(B)])
            # bootstraps are independent per model (not perfectly paired); conservative CI
            slope_rows.append(dict(cond=c, slope_pp_per_decade=sl, lo=np.percentile(bs, 2.5),
                                   hi=np.percentile(bs, 97.5),
                                   spearman_rho=pd.Series(y).corr(pd.Series(x), method="spearman")))
        slopes = pd.DataFrame(slope_rows)
        slopes.to_csv(f"{RES}/scale_slopes.csv", index=False)
        print("\nScale slopes (Qwen, pp per 10x params):\n", slopes.round(2))

    # ---------- calibration ----------
    cal_rows = []
    for m in models:
        for c in ["clean"] + CONDS:
            per = desc[(desc.model == m) & (desc.cond == c)]
            cal_rows.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, ece=per.ece.mean(), acc=per.acc.mean(),
                                 entropy=per.entropy.mean(), conf=per.conf.mean()))
    cal = pd.DataFrame(cal_rows)
    # bootstrap CI on ECE(cond)-ECE(clean), resampling items within task (paired)
    dci = []
    for m in models:
        gm = d[d.model == m]
        tasks = {t: gm[gm.task == t] for t in TASKS}
        ids = {t: g.test_id.unique() for t, g in tasks.items()}
        bucket = {(t, c): {i: g2 for i, g2 in g[g.cond == c].groupby("test_id")} for t, g in tasks.items()
                  for c in ["clean"] + CONDS}
        for c in CONDS:
            diffs = []
            for b in range(300):
                vals = []
                for t in TASKS:
                    s = rng.choice(ids[t], len(ids[t]))
                    gc = pd.concat([bucket[(t, "clean")][i] for i in s])
                    gx = pd.concat([bucket[(t, c)][i] for i in s])
                    vals.append(ece(gx.conf.values, gx.acc.values) - ece(gc.conf.values, gc.acc.values))
                diffs.append(np.mean(vals))
            pt = cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == c)].ece.item() - cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == "clean")].ece.item()
            dci.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, dECE=pt, lo=np.percentile(diffs, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(diffs, 97.5)))
    dci = pd.DataFrame(dci)
    cal.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration.csv", index=False)
    dci.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration_delta.csv", index=False)
    print("\nCalibration (equal-task mean):\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="ece").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nΔECE vs clean with CI:\n", dci.round(3).to_string(index=False))
    print("\nEntropy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="entropy").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nAccuracy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="acc").loc[models].round(3))

    # ---------- length interaction ----------
    w = d.pivot_table(index=["model", "task", "test_id", "T", "long_test"], columns="cond", values="predT").reset_index()
    w["dlen"] = w["length"] - w["clean"]
    li = w.groupby(["model", "long_test"]).dlen.mean().unstack() * 100
    li.columns = ["short_test", "long_test"]
    li["long_minus_short"] = li.long_test - li.short_test
    # bootstrap CI for long-minus-short
    lis = []
    for m in models:
        g = w[w.model == m]
        it = g.groupby(["task", "test_id", "long_test"]).dlen.mean().reset_index()
        L, S = it[it.long_test].dlen.values, it[~it.long_test].dlen.values
        bs = [L[rng.integers(0, len(L), len(L))].mean() - S[rng.integers(0, len(S), len(S))].mean() for _ in range(B)]
        lis.append((np.percentile(bs, 2.5) * 100, np.percentile(bs, 97.5) * 100))
    li = li.loc[models]
    li["lo"], li["hi"] = [a for a, _ in lis], [b for _, b in lis]
    li.to_csv(f"{RES}/length_interaction.csv")
    print("\nLength-condition Δ by test length (pp):\n", li.round(2))

    # ---------- figures ----------
    colors = {"skew": "#3b6fb6", "recency": "#d9822b", "primacy": "#5aa36c", "length": "#a35aa3"}
    # Fig 1: Δ by condition × model
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.2))
    n = len(CONDS); wdt = 0.8 / n
    for j, c in enumerate(CONDS):
        s = shifts[shifts.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        xs = np.arange(len(models)) + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * wdt
        ax.bar(xs, s.delta_pp, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c,
               yerr=[s.delta_pp - s.lo, s.hi - s.delta_pp], capsize=2, error_kw=dict(lw=0.8))
    ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6)
    ax.axhspan(15, 25, color=colors["skew"], alpha=0.08)
    ax.axhspan(8, 15, color=colors["recency"], alpha=0.08)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(models))); ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=15)
    ax.set_ylabel("Δ P(pred = target) vs clean (pp)")
    ax.set_title("Shift toward the manipulated label (mean of 4 tasks, 95% bootstrap CI)\n"
                 "shaded: hypothesised ranges (skew 15–25, recency 8–15)")
    ax.legend(ncol=4, frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig1_target_shift.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 2: scale curves per task (Qwen)
    if len(qwen) >= 2:
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 5, figsize=(16, 3.4), sharey=True)
        xs = [sizes[m] for m in qwen]
        for ax, t in zip(axes, ["mean"] + TASKS):
            for c in CONDS:
                s = shifts[shifts.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[qwen]
                y = s.delta_pp if t == "mean" else s[f"delta_{t}"]
                ax.plot(xs, y, "o-", color=colors[c], label=c)
                if t == "mean":
                    ax.fill_between(xs, s.lo, s.hi, color=colors[c], alpha=0.12)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
            ax.set_title("4-task mean" if t == "mean" else t); ax.set_xlabel("params (B)")
        axes[0].set_ylabel("Δ target rate (pp)"); axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
        fig.suptitle("Bias vs. model scale (Qwen2.5-Instruct ladder)", y=1.02)
        fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig2_scale.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(fig)

    # Fig 3: ΔECE and accuracy
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3.8))
    for j, c in enumerate(CONDS):
        s = dci[dci.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models]
        xs = np.arange(len(models)) + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * wdt
        axes[0].bar(xs, 100 * s.dECE, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c,
                    yerr=[100 * (s.dECE - s.lo), 100 * (s.hi - s.dECE)], capsize=2, error_kw=dict(lw=0.8))
        a = cal[cal.cond == c].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values - cal[cal.cond == "clean"].set_index("model").loc[models].acc.values
        axes[1].bar(xs, 100 * a, wdt, color=colors[c], label=c)
    for ax, yl in zip(axes, ["ΔECE vs clean (pp)", "Δ accuracy vs clean (pp)"]):
        ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6); ax.set_xticks(range(len(models)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=20, fontsize=8); ax.set_ylabel(yl)
    axes[0].legend(ncol=2, frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[0].set_title("Calibration error change"); axes[1].set_title("Accuracy change")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"{FIG}/fig3_calibration_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)
    print("figures written")

# ---------- calibration ----------
    cal_rows = []
    for m in models:
        for c in ["clean"] + CONDS:
            per = desc[(desc.model == m) & (desc.cond == c)]
            cal_rows.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, ece=per.ece.mean(), acc=per.acc.mean(),
                                 entropy=per.entropy.mean(), conf=per.conf.mean()))
    cal = pd.DataFrame(cal_rows)
    # bootstrap CI on ECE(cond)-ECE(clean), resampling items within task (paired)
    dci = []
    for m in models:
        gm = d[d.model == m]
        tasks = {t: gm[gm.task == t] for t in TASKS}
        ids = {t: g.test_id.unique() for t, g in tasks.items()}
        bucket = {(t, c): {i: g2 for i, g2 in g[g.cond == c].groupby("test_id")} for t, g in tasks.items()
                  for c in ["clean"] + CONDS}
        for c in CONDS:
            diffs = []
            for b in range(300):
                vals = []
                for t in TASKS:
                    s = rng.choice(ids[t], len(ids[t]))
                    gc = pd.concat([bucket[(t, "clean")][i] for i in s])
                    gx = pd.concat([bucket[(t, c)][i] for i in s])
                    vals.append(ece(gx.conf.values, gx.acc.values) - ece(gc.conf.values, gc.acc.values))
                diffs.append(np.mean(vals))
            pt = cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == c)].ece.item() - cal[(cal.model == m) & (cal.cond == "clean")].ece.item()
            dci.append(dict(model=m, cond=c, dECE=pt, lo=np.percentile(diffs, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(diffs, 97.5)))
    dci = pd.DataFrame(dci)
    cal.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration.csv", index=False)
    dci.to_csv(f"{RES}/calibration_delta.csv", index=False)
    print("\nCalibration (equal-task mean):\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="ece").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nΔECE vs clean with CI:\n", dci.round(3).to_string(index=False))
    print("\nEntropy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="entropy").loc[models].round(3))
    print("\nAccuracy:\n", cal.pivot(index="model", columns="cond", values="acc").loc[models].round(3))

    # ---------- length interaction ----------
    w = d.pivot_table(index=["model", "task", "test_id", "T", "long_test"], columns="cond", values="predT").reset_index()
    w["dlen"] = w["length"] - w["clean"]
    li = w.groupby(["model", "long_test"]).dlen.mean().unstack() * 100

# In-Context Learning Label Bias: When Demonstrations Teach the Wrong Lesson

## 1. Executive Summary

**Question.** When few-shot demonstrations carry a spurious statistic, how far do LLM predictions move toward the label that statistic favours? We test four such statistics: label frequency skew, recency, label position (primacy), and label-length correlation. We also ask whether the effect changes with model scale.

**Answer.** In modern instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B–14B; Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.1-8B), every one of these biases is much smaller than hypothesised. Across 80,000 scored prompts (8 models × 10,000):

- **Frequency skew (80/20)** is the largest bias in small models: +4 to +5 pp for small Qwen-Instruct, +8.9 pp for a 1.5B *base* model, and +16.9 pp for Llama-3.2-1B. It shrinks with scale to roughly zero at 14B (−0.6 pp) and 8B (+0.6 pp).
- **Recency** (last two demos share a label) does not produce the predicted 8–15 pp pull. From 3B upward it produces a small but significant *anti*-recency effect: −1.7 to −3.6 pp, Holm-corrected p < 0.05.
- **Label-length correlation** has no reliable effect at any size (|Δ| ≤ 3 pp; no model shows a length → label rule).
- **Calibration error (ECE)** does not increase reliably under any bias. All 32 ΔECE bootstrap CIs include or touch zero.

Shifts large enough to match the hypothesis appear only with extreme manipulations, mostly on the most ambiguous task (MRPC). Examples: 100% single-label demos give +16 to +36 pp in small models, and skew on MRPC gives +17 to +42 pp.

**Practical implication.** For current instruction-tuned models at ≥3B, the *specific* labels in a balanced-looking demo set matter less than ordinary demo-to-demo variance. Swapping one balanced demo set for another flips 4–23% of predictions, which is larger than any systematic bias we measured in ≥3B models. Practitioners should worry about ambiguous tasks and very small models, where skew still matters, and should average over demo sets rather than tune label order.

## 2. Research Question & Hypothesis

The hypothesis under test has five parts:

- **H1.** Frequency skew gives the largest bias: a 15–25 pp shift toward the majority label.
- **H2.** Recency gives the second largest: 8–15 pp.
- **H3.** Label-length correlation gives a moderate bias (5–10 pp) that is hard to overcome with scale.
- **H4.** Larger models partially correct frequency skew but amplify recency bias.
- **H5.** Calibration error increases monotonically with all bias types.

**Motivation / gap.** Zhao et al. (2021, *Calibrate Before Use*) documented majority-label and recency bias in GPT-3-era base models. Fei et al. (2023) added domain-label bias. Lu et al. (2022) showed that demonstration order matters. Those studies mostly varied one factor on older base models. Here all four manipulations are measured with one paired protocol, across a dense scale ladder of a modern instruction-tuned family plus a second family, and calibration is reported for each bias type. (Note: the resource-finder stage did not run for this workspace, so there was no `literature_review.md`, papers or code. The background above comes from known literature, not from downloaded PDFs.)

## 3. Experimental Setup

### Tasks and data
| Task | Type | Labels (verbalisers) | Test items | Demo pool |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SST-2 | sentiment | negative / positive | 200 from validation (100/100) | train, 5–60 words |
| RTE | NLI | yes (entail) / no | 200 from validation (100/100) | train, ≤80 words |
| AG News | topic, 4-way | World / Sports / Business / Technology | 200 from test (50 each) | train, ≤80 words |
| MRPC | paraphrase | no / yes | 200 from validation (100/100) | train, ≤70 words |

SST-2 and AG News come from the local HF cache. RTE and MRPC come from `nyu-mll/glue` parquet files (`datasets/raw/`). Demos come from train and test items from validation/test, so the two never overlap.

### Manipulations
Every prompt has k = 10 demonstrations. The *target label* T is rotated through every label, so a model's intrinsic label preference cancels out.

| Condition | Label counts | Order | Lengths |
|---|---|---|---|
| clean | balanced (5/5; 3/3/2/2 for AG News) | random | random |
| skew | 8 × T, 2 × other (80/20) | random | random |
| recency | balanced | last 2 demos = T | random |
| primacy (label-position) | balanced | first 2 demos = T | random |
| length | balanced | random | T demos from the longest third of T's pool, others from the shortest third (mean +15 to +29 words for T) |

"Label-position correlation (label always near sentence start)" was interpreted as *prompt-level* position (T demos placed first, i.e. primacy). That makes it the mirror image of recency.

Each (task, item, T, condition) gets its own seeded demo sample. This gives 10,000 prompts, and every model sees exactly the same prompts.

**Supplementary dose-response set** (`prompts_supp.jsonl`, 6,000 prompts): skew at 60% and 100%, and recency with the last 4 demos = T. In AG News, recency4 necessarily raises T's share to 40%.

Prompt format (raw completion, no chat template), shown for SST-2:
```
Classify the sentiment of each movie review as positive or negative.

Review: <demo text>
Sentiment: positive

... (10 demos) ...
Review: <test text>
Sentiment:
```

### Models
All models run locally with vLLM 0.32 (bf16 unless noted), greedy decoding, on a single shared RTX A6000 (48 GB) slice per run:

- Qwen2.5-Instruct: 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, **7B-AWQ** (4-bit), 14B
- Qwen2.5-1.5B **base** (to test the effect of instruction tuning)
- Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4

The 7B and 8B models had to use 4-bit AWQ checkpoints because other users' jobs left ≤17 GB free on the shared GPUs. No API keys were available on this host, and the task asked for local models. vLLM was used instead of Ollama because it exposes exact label log-probabilities.

**Scoring.** Each prompt is scored by the next-token distribution restricted to the first token of each label word (with leading space), renormalised over the label set (`allowed_token_ids` + `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"`). The prediction is the argmax. This removes format and parsing failures and yields probabilities for calibration.

### Metrics
- **Target shift Δ** (primary): P(pred = T | condition) − P(pred = T | clean), paired on (task, item, T), in percentage points. It is averaged over T and items, then over the 4 tasks with equal weight.
- Accuracy and Δaccuracy, both overall and split by whether gold = T.
- **ECE**: 10 equal-width bins on max-probability confidence, computed per task and then averaged.
- Normalised predictive entropy.
- Mean probability mass on T (a soft version of Δ).
- **Noise floor**: the flip rate between two independent clean demo sets for the same item.

### Statistics
- 95% CIs come from a cluster bootstrap over test items, resampled within each task (2,000 resamples; 1,000 for ΔECE, paired).
- Significance uses sign-flip permutation tests on per-item Δ, Holm-corrected over all 32 (model × condition) tests.
- Scale trend: OLS slope of Δ on log10(params) along the Qwen-Instruct ladder, plus Spearman ρ across the 5 sizes.

Seeds: demo sampling is seeded by an md5 hash of (task, item, T, condition); vLLM seed = 0; analysis RNG seed = 0.
